subject: Cloud Computing
title: Global Databases
description: A fast breakdown of Global Databases for builders.

hook.text: Google Spanner is a database that spans the entire planet. It uses atomic clocks to keep data consistent.

buildup.text: Global databases replicate data across continents, giving every user fast, local access with strong consistency.

discovery.text: Spanner, CockroachDB, and Cosmos DB offer globally distributed databases, solving the latency vs. consistency dilemma.

twist.text: Global databases are expensive and complex. Most applications don't need planetary-scale data distribution.

climax.text: They're built for apps with truly global users: messaging, gaming, and financial services that need speed everywhere.

punchline.text: Global databases span the planet. Most apps don't need that yet.

quiz.question: How does Google Spanner maintain consistency across continents?
options: It uses atomic clocks to precisely synchronize data across global replicas
It only allows writes from one continent at a time
Data is stored in a single data center and cached everywhere else

details.summary: Global databases replicate data across multiple regions worldwide, enabling low-latency reads from any region and resilience against regional outages. Google Spanner, Cosmos DB, and Aurora Global Database offer different consistency and latency tradeoffs.
details.whyItMatters: Applications serving global users need data close to every user. Global databases solve this without building custom replication, which is one of the hardest problems in distributed systems.
takeaways: Data is replicated across regions for low-latency global reads
Provides resilience against full regional cloud outages
Google Spanner offers strong global consistency uniquely

faq.question: How does Google Spanner achieve global consistency?
faq.answer: Spanner uses TrueTime, a globally synchronized clock based on GPS and atomic clocks in every data center. This gives transactions globally consistent timestamps, enabling strong consistency across regions without the performance penalties of traditional distributed consensus.

faq.question: What are the costs of global databases?
faq.answer: Global databases charge for compute and storage in each region plus cross-region replication bandwidth. Costs can be three to five times higher than single-region deployments. The expense is justified only for applications requiring global low-latency access or regional failover.
